Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals · Section 15.7 · Exercise 31

Six Orders of Integration under a Slanted Plane and above a Parabolic Wall

Problem

Express the triple integral

∭E​f(x,y,z)dV

as an iterated integral in six different ways, where E is the solid bounded by the surfaces y=x2, z=0, and y+2z=4.

Reading the solid

The three surfaces play three different roles. The floor is the plane z=0. The roof is the plane y+2z=4, which we can write as z=2−y/2. The wall is the parabolic cylinder y=x2, whose rulings are parallel to the z-axis.

The word “bounded” fixes the side of each surface. The solid lies above the floor, so z≥0. It lies below the roof, so y+2z≤4. It lies on the side of the wall where y is larger than x2, so y≥x2. A point is therefore in E exactly when

y≥x2,z≥0,y+2z≤4.

These three conditions have a useful consequence. The roof gives y≤4−2z≤4, and the wall gives x2≤y, so x2≤4, that is, −2≤x≤2. The solid is thus confined to a slab of width 4, and its two ends are the flat cross-sections at x=−2 and x=2.

At a fixed value of x, the cross-section is the part of the yz-plane with

x2≤y≤4,0≤z≤2−y/2.

This region is a trapezoid. Its top edge is the line z=2−y/2, its bottom edge is the segment z=0 from y=x2 to y=4, and its left edge is the segment y=x2 from z=0 to z=2−x2/2. At x=0 the left edge collapses and the trapezoid becomes the triangle 0≤y≤4, 0≤z≤2−y/2.

The solid tapers toward positive y. At y=4 the roof height is 2−4/2=0, so the roof touches the floor along the segment y=4, z=0, −2≤x≤2. That segment is the sharp edge of the solid.

For integration we also need the projection of E on the xy-plane. Drop z. The conditions on x and y become x2≤y≤4, which describes the region between the parabola and the line y=4. Figure 2 shows this projection and one cross-section.

Solution

Step 1 — Choose the innermost variable

An order of integration names the innermost variable first and the outermost variable last. The inner limits may depend on the two variables that are still free. Here the wall ties x to y, and the roof ties z to y. The choice of the innermost variable therefore controls the shape of the inner limits.

If z is innermost, the floor and the roof supply the inner limits, 0≤z≤2−y/2, and the remaining limits come from the wall. If y is innermost, the wall and the roof supply the inner limits, x2≤y≤4−2z. If x is innermost, the wall supplies the inner limits, −y​≤x≤y​.

The six orders fall into three groups of two. Each group has the same inner variable. The middle and outer variables can be exchanged, but the middle limits must then be rewritten for the new outer variable.

Step 2 — Inner variable z

Order dzdydx. Hold x and y fixed. The floor is below and the roof is above, so z runs from 0 to 2−y/2. Next, at the fixed x, the variable y runs from the wall to the edge, x2≤y≤4. Last, x runs over the width of the solid, −2≤x≤2.

∫−22​∫x24​∫02−y/2​f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Order dzdxdy. The inner limits are the same, because they depend only on the fixed value of y. The variable x now comes next. At the fixed y, the wall gives −y​≤x≤y​. The outer variable y runs from 0 to 4, because the extreme point of the solid has y=4.

∫04​∫−y​y​​∫02−y/2​f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Step 3 — Inner variable y

Order dydzdx. Hold x and z fixed. The point lies to the right of the wall and below the roof, so x2≤y≤4−2z. Next, at the fixed x, the variable z runs from the floor to the roof, 0≤z≤2−x2/2. Last, x runs from −2 to 2.

∫−22​∫02−x2/2​∫x24−2z​f(x,y,z)dydzdx

Order dydxdz. The inner limits still depend only on the fixed value of z. The variable x now comes next. The wall gives x2≤y, and the inner limits already force y≤4−2z, so x2≤4−2z and −4−2z​≤x≤4−2z​. The outer variable z runs from 0 to 2, the height of the roof at y=0.

∫02​∫−4−2z​4−2z​​∫x24−2z​f(x,y,z)dydxdz

Step 4 — Inner variable x

Order dxdydz. Hold y and z fixed. The wall gives −y​≤x≤y​. The middle variable is y. At the fixed z, the roof requires y≤4−2z, so 0≤y≤4−2z. The outer variable z runs from 0 to 2.

∫02​∫04−2z​∫−y​y​​f(x,y,z)dxdydz

Order dxdzdy. The inner limits are again −y​≤x≤y​. The middle variable is now z. At the fixed y, the floor and the roof give 0≤z≤2−y/2. The outer variable y runs from 0 to 4.

∫04​∫02−y/2​∫−y​y​​f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

Step 5 — Check every order with a test integrand

Set f=1. Each of the six integrals then gives the volume of E. The order dzdydx computes it in three stages. The inner integral is the height of the roof above the floor

∫02−y/2​1dz=2−2y​.

The middle integral is the area of the trapezoid at the fixed x

∫x24​(2−2y​)dy=4x4​−2x2+4.

The outer integral adds these areas over the width of the solid

∫−22​(4x4​−2x2+4)dx=15128​≈8.533.

SymPy evaluates the six iterated integrals of Step 2 through Step 4. Every order returns 128/15. A second test with f=y2z2, which weights the region near the roof and far from the wall, returns 65536/9009≈7.275 for every order. Table 1 lists the six values.

OrderValue for f=1Value for f=y2z2
dzdydx128/1565536/9009
dzdxdy128/1565536/9009
dydzdx128/1565536/9009
dydxdz128/1565536/9009
dxdydz128/1565536/9009
dxdzdy128/1565536/9009

Answer

For E={(x,y,z):x2≤y≤4, 0≤z≤2−y/2}, the integral ∭E​fdV has the six forms below.

Inner variable z:

∫−22​∫x24​∫02−y/2​f(x,y,z)dzdydx
∫04​∫−y​y​​∫02−y/2​f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Inner variable y:

∫−22​∫02−x2/2​∫x24−2z​f(x,y,z)dydzdx
∫02​∫−4−2z​4−2z​​∫x24−2z​f(x,y,z)dydxdz

Inner variable x:

∫02​∫04−2z​∫−y​y​​f(x,y,z)dxdydz
∫04​∫02−y/2​∫−y​y​​f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

All six orders give the same value for every integrand. For f=1, each order gives the volume 128/15≈8.533.

Notation

SymbolMeaning
∭E​fdVThe triple integral of the function f over the three-dimensional solid E. It is the limit of sums of values of f times small volumes.
EThe solid region of integration, that is, the set of points (x,y,z) that satisfy all three defining inequalities.
f(x,y,z)The integrand, an arbitrary function of the three coordinates.
dVThe volume element. In Cartesian coordinates dV=dxdydz.
dzdydxAn order of integration. The innermost differential is written first and the outermost is written last.
y=x2A parabolic cylinder that acts as the wall. It contains every line parallel to the z-axis through a point of the parabola y=x2 in the xy-plane.
z=0The floor, which is the xy-plane.
y+2z=4The roof. Solved for z, it is z=2−y/2, a plane that falls by 1/2 unit for each unit of y.
2−y/2The height of the roof above the floor at a fixed y.
4−2zThe largest value of y inside the solid at a fixed z. It is the value where the roof height equals z.
y​The nonnegative square root. At a fixed y, it is the half-width of the solid in the x-direction.
x2≤y≤4The projection of E on the xy-plane, which is the region between the parabola and the line y=4.
128/15, 65536/9009The exact values of the six integrals for f=1 and for f=y2z2. Their decimals are 8.533 and 7.275.

Verification

Four scripts support the result. Run each one from calculus-15.7.31/solution.

  • part1_step1.py checks eight sample points against the three inequalities and computes the volume from the order dzdydx. It obtains 2−y/2, then x4/4−2x2+4 for the trapezoid area, then 128/15≈8.533 for the volume. It also checks the trapezoid area as the large triangle minus the removed part.
  • part1_step2.py evaluates all six orders with SymPy. Every order gives 128/15 for f=1 and 65536/9009 for f=y2z2.
  • part1_step3.py evaluates all six orders a second time with nested mpmath quadrature. The twelve numerical values agree with the exact values to all sixteen printed digits.
  • part1_figure1.py draws the three boundary surfaces. part1_figure2.py draws the projection on the xy-plane and the trapezoid cross-section.
